content.title: Not on the Space Coast? Here's when you'll see and hear NASA's Artemis II launch tonight across Florida
content.text: The Lake County Sheriff's Office confirms the deputy who shot and killed a Leesburg man while responding to a stabbing incident did not have his body camera on the moment he fired his gun."He (the deputy) did not activate his blue lights, which would have in turn activated his body camera," the release said. "He simply pulled up to the scene and was quickly pointed in the direction where Mr. Reed (the stabbing suspect) had gone."The family identified Timotheus Reed, 38, as the man who was shot and killed Sunday in the Montclair area of Leesburg by an LCSO Deputy."Where there's been a stabbing, or if there's a serious crime, you would think they'd want the body camera on to protect themselves," Reed's sister Charity Mann said. Reed was transported to Orlando Regional Medical Center, where he later died.Deputies said they were responding to the block after a dispatcher received a 911 call from a bystander reporting a stabbing.The sheriff's office has released that audio."He's bleeding. He's been stabbed in the neck," the caller can be heard telling the dispatcher.According to Reed's family, he had gotten into an altercation with a cousin, but that cousin claims he only had scratch marks on his face, and Reed never stabbed him. On Monday, the LCSO released body camera video the deputy recorded of the aftermath of the shooting, showing Reed lying on the ground as deputies tend to him.The video does not show the moments before or during the shooting.The sheriff's office said that while it cannot release the name of the deputy, it can share that "he was hired in April 2023 to work in Corrections in our jail and then in January 2025, he transferred to the Law Enforcement side as a patrol deputy. During his time here, he has received an exceptional notice for his work in the jail; the only disciplinary action he has received was a written reprimand for an at-fault traffic crash."The LCSO said an autopsy showed Reed died of a single gunshot wound to the abdomen. "My message to them is that we want answers," Mann said. "We want accountability."Reed's family and dozens of community members gathered outside the Lake County Sheriff's Office on Wednesday morning, demanding to speak with someone from LCSO and for the agency to release the remainder of the body camera video."There was no reason for him to open fire when he was not in danger," Reed's sister, Christina Eliscard, said.The protesters went inside the sheriff's office lobby, marched to the front of the county administrative building, and then continued the demonstration, chanting, "No justice, no peace," inside the Lake County Historical Museum. Although LCSO sent out a release saying there wasn't more video to release, Reed's family had their doubts."We don't believe that," said Reed's father, Pastor Clay Reed. "We don't believe that because that's not how law enforcement works. That's not how it works. We see, we see body cams on a simple traffic stop, how in the world is a deadly situation taking place, and there's no body camera." Pastor Reed said his family has retained civil rights attorney Benjamin Crump as they seek justice for his son, who was the father of five children. The deputy was placed on administrative leave pending the outcome of the investigation by the Florida Department of Law Enforcement."At this time, our agency has an open administrative investigation that will parallel the investigation being conducted by the Florida Department of Law Enforcement," the LCSO said in the release. "The purpose of our investigation is to determine whether the shooting was consistent with agency policy and training, while the investigation by the Florida Department of Law Enforcement is to determine whether the deputy's actions were within the statutory provisions for use of force by a law enforcement officer."Lake County Sheriff's Office guidelines and procedures:>> Below is the LCSO's full list of policies for the use of recording equipment and the control and storage of information obtained on the recordings.
